title: Takeoff Ground Run Distance
conditions: Wing flaps 15°, paved/level/dry runway, full throttle and max RPM, takeoff speed = 80 MPH IAS

exampleCheck.note: Worked example printed on the chart (points A-F). Re-measured directly from reference/fig5-06-takeoff-ground-run.png pixel positions on 2026-10-01, superseding an earlier pass that measured B/D/F correctly as pixel ROW values but had wrong axis calibration (used the wrong top-of-chart reference value, which inflated every reading) and never independently checked the example's actual weight/wind inputs, inheriting an assumed weightLb=3100/windMph=10 from a sibling chart. Correct right-axis calibration is 2400 ft at row 404 and 400 ft at row 886 (not the previously assumed box-edge values). Correct example inputs, read directly off the dashed line's crossing of the weight and wind axes: weight=3000 lb (point C sits on the '30' gridline, not '31'), wind=30 mph headwind (point F sits on the '30' gridline, not '10'). Measured B=1439 ft, D=1018 ft, F=850 ft; weightExponent and windKPerMph refit from these with the corrected weight/wind magnitudes. Model reproduces the worked example to within 0.02%.

unverifiedAltitudes.note: The 0/2000/4000/8000 ft altitudeCurves entries below are the ORIGINAL, unverified digitization. Only the 6000 ft entry (above) and the weight/wind exponents have been independently re-measured pixel-by-pixel against the source chart. A reliable automated trace of the other four curves was not achieved in this pass — they cross near a steep 'STD TEMP' reference line on the chart that repeatedly caused the curve-tracer to jump between curves, and disambiguating each one visually would need more time than this pass allowed. Given the 6000 ft entry was off by ~2x, these others likely carry similar error and should be re-checked before being trusted for altitudes other than 6000 ft.
